newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas extends losses late to settle lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas extends losses late to settle lower.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended near session lows Monday after April failed to break through resistance earlier in the session, industry sources said.

Despite some late technical selling, April remained range-bound before settling 5.1 cents lower at $1.909 mmBtu. It had reached a high of $2.00 early in the session. May finished down 7.3 cents at $1.948.
Most traders blamed the softness before the close on technical selling after April showed reluctance to break through $2.
"There is just no reason why April, a shoulder month, should move any higher. Unless we get some real weather, we'll probably see some downward movement before its expiration," one trader said.

After $2, technical traders still pegged resistance in April at $2.04, then in the mid-teens and at $2.28. If April breaks through $1.88, traders said next support was likely at $1.78-1.80 and the $1.701 contract low.

In the cash market, Gulf Coast prices on average were four cents higher in the mid-$1.90s to low-$2 area despite some late softening. Prices on the Midcontinent pipes were also slightly higher in the low-$1.90s, with Detroit city-gate quoted around $2.20. At the New York city-gate, prices were talked firmer in the mid-to-high $2.30s, while Appalachian prices inched up two cents to $2.11-2.16.

In its afternoon report, Weather Services Corp was calling for below- to much below-normal temperatures in the eastern U.S. Wednesday through Friday. Colder weather in the Great Lakes states is expected to arrive Tuesday and Wednesday. However, temperatures about six- to 12-degrees above normal are expected to continue in the western half of the U.S., Weather Services Corp said.
The 12-month strip fell five cents to $2.065. NYMEX said an estimated 34,290 Henry Hub contracts traded, up sharply from Friday's revised tally of 17,357.
No NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas traded.

On the KCBT, April settled at the lower end of today's range at $1.705, down 3.5 cents. Deferreds were one to 5.5 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.3 cents to 20.2 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical cash prices in the Permian Basin were talked steady to a couple of cents higher in the low-to-mid $1.80s, while Waha gas traded mostly in the high-$1.80s.
